title: Microsoft Warns Windows 11 Update Causes Black Screen and Desktop Loading Issues
content_md: Microsoft has confirmed a Windows 11 issue that can leave users staring at a black screen after sign-in or prevent the desktop from loading automatically. The problem is linked to the August 2026 non-security preview update for Windows 11 version 26H1, KB5120996, and may also affect devices that installed later cumulative updates. Microsoft said the fault has been seen primarily in virtual desktop environments, particularly Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) session hosts using FSLogix profile-management technology. Microsoft Warns Windows 11 Update Causes Black Screen Microsoft lists the issue as mitigated, but a permanent code fix is still expected in a future Windows update. Affected users may sign in successfully but encounter a blank black screen instead of a usable Windows desktop. In other cases, the desktop session fails to start automatically, blocking access to the taskbar, Start menu, desktop icons, and normal shell functions. Microsoft said Windows Explorer crashes can appear in the Application event logs on affected devices. Explorer is the Windows shell process responsible for rendering much of the interactive desktop experience, including the taskbar and File Explorer. When it does not start correctly after logon, users can be left with an apparently unresponsive black display even though their session is running.
